person.name: Friedensreich_Hundertwasser
person.summary: Friedrich Stowasser, better known as Friedensreich Regentag Dunkelbunt Hundertwasser, was an Austrian visual artist and architect noted for vivid colors, biomorphic forms, and ecological advocacy. He opposed straight lines and standardization, and later settled in the Far North of New Zealand, where he lived and worked for much of his life.

events.title: Birth in Vienna
events.description: Friedrich Stowasser was born in Vienna, Austria; he would later be known as Friedensreich Regentag Dunkelbunt Hundertwasser.

events.date_note: During the Nazi era in Austria, he and his Jewish mother posed as Christians; he also joined the Hitler Youth to remain inconspicuous
events.title: Surviving the Nazi era in Austria
events.description: Hundertwasser and his mother avoided persecution by presenting themselves as Christians; he has described himself as "half-Jewish."

events.date_note: He studied for three months after World War II; the exact months are not specified
events.title: Postwar study at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna; adopts the name "Hundertwasser"
events.description: After the war he spent three months at the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna. Around this time he began signing his works as "Hundertwasser" rather than "Stowasser."
locations: Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, Vienna, Austria

location_coordinates.label: Academy of Fine Arts, 3, Schillerplatz, Innere Stadt, Vienna, 1010, Austria
location_coordinates.name: Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, Vienna, Austria

events.title: First commercial exhibition success in Vienna
events.description: He achieved his first commercial success with a painting exhibition in Vienna.

events.title: Mouldiness Manifesto against Rationalism in Architecture
events.description: At Seckau Monastery he read his "Mouldiness Manifesto," rejecting straight lines and functionalist architecture, and asserting ideas like the "Window Right."

events.title: Establishes home at "Hahnsäge" in the Waldviertel
events.description: He bought "Hahnsäge," a former sawmill in Lower Austria's sparsely populated Waldviertel, creating a home close to nature.

events.title: Painting period in Uganda's Tooro Kingdom
events.description: Hundertwasser spent time in the Tooro Kingdom in Uganda, creating works named for the kingdom, including his "Kingdom of the Toro" series.

location_coordinates.label: Tooro Kingdom Palace - Karuzika Palace, Fort Portal - Kasese Road, Fort Portal City, Kabarole, Western Region, Uganda
location_coordinates.name: Tooro Kingdom, Uganda

events.title: Incorporates Grüner Janura AG in Switzerland
events.description: He established the stock company Grüner Janura AG in Switzerland to manage his intellectual property (later renamed Namida AG).

events.date_note: In the 1970s he acquired several properties in the Bay of Islands and began living there largely self-sufficiently
events.title: Moves toward self-sufficient living in New Zealand's Far North
events.description: Hundertwasser acquired land in the Kaurinui Valley, Bay of Islands, designed the "Bottle House," and experimented with grass roofs, solar power, and biological water purification.
locations: Kaurinui Valley, Bay of Islands, Te Tai Tokerau (Northland), New Zealand

events.title: Hundertwasser Day in Washington, D.C.
events.description: Supporting Ralph Nader’s anti-nuclear efforts, he planted trees in Judiciary Square; Mayor Marion Barry proclaimed 18 November "Hundertwasser Day."
locations: Judiciary Square, Washington, D.C., United States

location_coordinates.label: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
location_coordinates.name: Washington, D.C., United States

location_coordinates.label: Judiciary Square, E Street Northwest, Downtown East, Ward 6, Washington, District of Columbia, 20554, United States
location_coordinates.name: Judiciary Square, Washington, D.C., United States

events.title: Birth of his only child, Heidi Trimmel
events.description: Hundertwasser's daughter, Heidi Trimmel, was born.

events.title: Designs the Koru flag for New Zealand
events.description: He created his koru flag design, using the Māori koru spiral to symbolize new life, growth, strength, and peace.

events.title: Hundertwasserhaus in Vienna completed
events.description: His best-known architectural work, the Hundertwasserhaus apartment block in Vienna—with undulating floors, a grass-covered roof, and trees growing from rooms—was completed and opened to residents.

events.title: Designs arts centre for Whangārei
events.description: Hundertwasser was invited to design an arts centre in Whangārei and completed the design; the project was not realized during his lifetime.

location_coordinates.label: Whangārei, Whangārei District, Northland, 0110, New Zealand
location_coordinates.name: Whangārei, New Zealand

events.title: Begins "Die Grüne Zitadelle von Magdeburg"
events.description: He started his final architectural project, Die Grüne Zitadelle von Magdeburg, in eastern Germany.

events.title: Death at sea; burial in New Zealand
events.description: Hundertwasser died of a heart attack aboard the Queen Elizabeth 2 in the Pacific Ocean. He was buried on his New Zealand property in the "Garden of the Happy Dead" under a tulip tree, according to his wishes.
locations: Garden of the Happy Dead, Kaurinui Valley, Bay of Islands, New Zealand
